name: Teotihuacan
description: Teotihuacan is a vast pre-Columbian city in the Valley of Mexico, approximately 40 km northeast of Mexico City, that was one of the largest cities in the ancient world at its peak (c. 100,000–200,000 inhabitants around 400–500 CE); its builders remain unknown, and the city features extraordinary astronomical alignments, a 100-meter ritual tunnel sealed for 2,000 years, and evidence of collective governance unlike other ancient civilizations.
full_description: Teotihuacan is located in the Valley of Mexico, approximately 40 kilometers northeast of modern Mexico City, in the State of Mexico (coordinates: 19°41'33"N, 98°50'38"W). At its height between 400 and 500 CE, it was among the largest cities in the ancient world, with an estimated population of 100,000 to 200,000 people — comprising 80–90% of the Valley of Mexico's population — making it the sixth-largest city in the world at that time. The city covers approximately 8 to 21 square kilometers and features a central 4-kilometer boulevard (the Avenue of the Dead, 40 meters wide), the massive Pyramid of the Sun (third-largest pyramid in the world by base area: 219.4 × 231.6 meters, 65 meters tall), the Pyramid of the Moon, and the Temple of the Feathered Serpent (Quetzalcoatl) with its associated underground tunnel system. The city's builders and original ethnic identity remain subjects of scholarly debate; candidates include Nahuas, Otomi, Totonac, or a multi-ethnic founding population. Uniquely among ancient civilizations, there is no evidence of a centralized monarchy at Teotihuacan: no royal palaces, no ceremonial ball courts, and no depictions of conquest or individual rulers in the artistic record, suggesting some form of collective governance. The city declined around 550–650 CE, with evidence of burning concentrated on elite structures (suggesting internal uprising or civil strife rather than external conquest), correlated with climate changes of 535–536 CE and possible drought-induced famine. The city was rediscovered and named by the Aztecs (Mexica) centuries after its abandonment; the Nahuatl name Teōtīhuacān means 'birthplace of the gods.' It was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987.

aliases.name: Teohuacan
aliases.meaning: proposed alternate original name meaning 'City of the Sun' (scholarly debate, 2018)

aliases.name: Puh
aliases.meaning: Place of Reeds — Maya designation for the city found in Maya texts

aliases.name: Teōtīhuacān
aliases.meaning: Birthplace of the gods — name given by the Aztecs who arrived after the city's abandonment

regions: State of Mexico (municipio de San Juan Teotihuacan)
origin: Single location in the Valley of Mexico, but cultural influence extended across Mesoamerica during the city's peak period (1–650 CE).

etymology.origin: Nahuatl language (Aztec), applied to the already-abandoned city when the Aztecs encountered it.
etymology.meaning: 'Birthplace of the gods' (Nahuatl: teōtl = god + ihuan = among + can = place). A 2018 scholarly proposal suggests the original name may have been 'Teohuacan' meaning 'City of the Sun.' The Maya texts reference the city as 'Puh' (Place of Reeds).
etymology.first_use: The Nahuatl name was applied by the Aztecs after approximately 1300 CE. The original name used by the city's inhabitants is unknown.

timeline.event: City of Teotihuacan begins rapid urban development; estimated 60,000–80,000 inhabitants
timeline.significance: Founding of the city as an urban center

timeline.event: Construction of the Pyramid of the Sun and early phases of the Pyramid of the Moon
timeline.significance: Creation of the city's most iconic structures

timeline.event: Warlord Sihyaj K'ahk', carrying feathered-serpent imagery associated with Teotihuacan, conquers Tikal and installs a new Maya king
timeline.significance: Direct evidence of Teotihuacan military and political influence over the Maya lowlands

timeline.event: K'inich Yax K'uk' Mo' establishes the Copán dynasty in Honduras with Teotihuacan backing
timeline.significance: Further evidence of Teotihuacan's wide political reach

timeline.event: Major burning event: elite residential compounds and temples selectively burned; evidence points to internal uprising or civil strife rather than external conquest
timeline.significance: Turning point in the city's decline

timeline.event: City effectively abandoned; population dispersed into surrounding region
timeline.significance: End of Teotihuacan as a major urban center

timeline.event: Major excavation project conducted by Leopoldo Batres under Mexican government direction; significant site alteration
timeline.significance: Early modern archaeological investigation, though methods now considered damaging

timeline.event: Man-made tunnel discovered beneath the Pyramid of the Sun during installation of a sound-and-light system
timeline.significance: Discovery of underground architecture beneath the largest pyramid

timeline.event: Teotihuacan designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site
timeline.significance: International recognition of the site's outstanding universal value

timeline.event: A sinkhole forms after a rainstorm above a sealed tunnel beneath the Temple of the Feathered Serpent; excavation by Sergio Gómez Chávez (Tlalocan Project) begins
timeline.significance: Discovery of the most artifact-rich archaeological context at the site

timeline.event: Excavation of the Feathered Serpent tunnel yields approximately 75,000 artifact fragments: wooden masks with jade/quartz inlay, pyrite spheres, greenstone figurines, miniature liquid mercury lakes, and four greenstone statues in original positions
timeline.significance: Most significant archaeological discovery at Teotihuacan in decades
timeline.source: Gómez Chávez, S. et al., INAH reports 2015

timeline.event: An approximately 1,800-year-old flower bouquet discovered in the Feathered Serpent tunnel — the first well-preserved plant matter found at the site
timeline.significance: Extraordinary preservation providing new insight into ritual deposits

related.name: Chichen Itza
related.description: Maya city that shows strong Teotihuacan cultural and architectural influence

related.name: Tikal
related.description: Maya city conquered by a Teotihuacan-affiliated warlord in 378 CE; significant Teotihuacan cultural presence documented

related.name: Nazca Lines
related.description: Another pre-Columbian archaeological phenomenon in South America associated with astronomical alignments and unknown purpose

cultural_notes: The Aztecs who encountered the abandoned city were so awed by its scale that they named it the birthplace of the gods and incorporated it into their own cosmology. The city's astronomical alignments suggest its builders had sophisticated cosmological beliefs that shaped the city's entire layout.

sources.title: Pre-Hispanic City of Teotihuacan — UNESCO World Heritage
